classes.name: Proton pump inhibitors
classes.description: Proton pump inhibitors: omeprazole (Prilosec), pantoprazole (Protonix), esomeprazole (Nexium), lansoprazole (Prevacid, SoluTab), rabeprazole (Aciphex), dexlansoprazole (Dexilant), omeprazole/sodium bicarbonate (Zegerid, Konvomep). Capsules, tablets, packets and suspensions. Not H2 blockers or vonoprazan.
classes.plainDescription: A once-a-day pill that shuts down most stomach acid. Used for reflux, ulcers and to protect the stomach.
classes.indication: GERD, erosive esophagitis, ulcers, H. pylori

classes.name: Potassium-competitive acid blocker
classes.description: Vonoprazan (Voquezna tablets; Voquezna Triple Pak and Dual Pak for H. pylori). Brand only, no generic. Usually a step after PPIs. If the plan lists no vonoprazan, that is the finding: pick Voquezna as the reference product and record the barrier.
classes.plainDescription: A newer brand-name acid blocker, used when the usual acid pills haven't worked.
classes.indication: Erosive esophagitis, heartburn from GERD, H. pylori

classes.name: H2 blockers
classes.description: Histamine-2 receptor antagonists: famotidine (Pepcid; tablets, suspension), cimetidine, nizatidine. Prescription strengths. Not PPIs.
classes.plainDescription: A milder acid pill, often taken at bedtime or as needed.
